regime_context: The detector is in a classic risk-off, defensive regime: Big Pharma is the headline narrative (rank 2, eligibility true, durability 0.84, full breadth, crowded, confirming), and the top seven eligible themes are all Healthcare, Defensive, or Staples — every high-rank eligible name is crowded. Rotation breadth is narrowing (0.39 eligible), the handoff from Memory/HBM to Big Pharma is wide at 0.559, and the only validated edge is the absolute-trend gate, which means defensive strength is real and durable but NOT alpha. AI/tech themes dominate the macro narrative headlines yet are deeply ineligible and at the bottom of the ranks — a sharp divergence between what is talked about and what is trending.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the Memory/HBM theme's absolute-trend gate re-engages (eligibility flips back to true and breadth rises above 0.5) — that would mark a return of the risk-on tech handoff; until then its rank-1 score is a stale attention signal, not a tradeable trend.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the confirmed leader on every coincident leg: top eligible rank, highest durability_bar (0.84) among leaders, true hurst trend, perfect breadth (1.0), and a 'confirming' val_state. The absolute-trend gate — the only validated edge — is showing defensive leadership precisely when it matters most for drawdown control. This supports a stay-with-the-trend lean, not a return forecast.
evidence: rank 2 among eligible, score 1.153, headline narrative
durability_bar 0.84 and hurst_tag 'trend' – high trend health
breadth 1.0 – full participation, durable rather than single-name
eligible true – passes the absolute-trend gate
theses.dissent: Crowding z of 1.46 plus 'crowded: true' means this is exactly the exhausted, overloved defensive trade that typically stalls; equal-weight Healthcare (XLV) and Staples are similarly crowded, suggesting a crowded defensive rotation that has little room left without a fresh macro shock.

falsifier.text: PPH falls below its 50-day average and stays there for 10 consecutive trading days

theses.subject: Consumer Staples (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Staples is the same defensive-trend story one rung down the ladder: eligible, trend, high durability (0.80), strong breadth (0.879). It is the cleanest scorable companion to Big Pharma, and the absolute-trend gate confirms the defensive rotation is broad rather than a single-name idiosyncrasy. This is a duration-preserving lean, not a prediction of outperformance.
evidence: crowded true at z 1.89 – confirming the risk-off rotation is consensus
theses.dissent: At a crowding z of 1.89, Staples is the single most crowded theme in the entire eligible set — the marginal buyer has already arrived, and any risk-on pulse (e.g., an AI headline spike) would unwind this fastest.

falsifier.text: XLP lags the S&P 500 by 3% over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Magnificent Seven
theses.thesis: The Mag7 shows a textbook risk-off divergence: macro narrative is dominated by AI/tech (7 of 18 recent headlines), yet the Mag7 theme is mediocre in rank (21), only marginally eligible with a durability of 0.65 and weak breadth (0.429). The absolute-trend gate has not confirmed leadership here, and with unscheduled_share at 1.0, this is pure headline risk, not a durable trend. Avoid until the trend gate re-engages.
evidence: breadth 0.429 – only a few names carrying any trend
macro narrative dominant theme is ai_tech (n=7) but Mag7 is not confirming
unscheduled_share 1.0 – every recent macro signal is unplanned noise
theses.dissent: If AI earnings or a scheduled catalyst re-ignites the Mag7, the low crowding (z 0.06) means there is plenty of room for a sharp catch-up that this avoid call would miss entirely.

falsifier.text: QQQ closes above its prior 60-day high and Big Pharma's durability_bar drops below 0.70 within the same window

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
